subject: commerce
title: ZIMSEC O-Level Commerce

officialDocument.title: Commerce Syllabus, Forms 1 - 4, 2015 - 2022 (Ministry of Primary and Secondary Education, Curriculum Development and Technical Services), examined by ZIMSEC at O Level
officialDocument.publisher: Ministry of Primary and Secondary Education (Curriculum Development and Technical Services) / Zimbabwe School Examinations Council (ZIMSEC)

sourceNote: Topic names and the numbers 6.1 to 6.11 are transcribed from the scope and sequence (6.0) of the Ministry's Commerce Syllabus Forms 1 - 4 (2015 - 2022); the sub-topics are the scope-and-sequence items for Forms 1 to 4, and the competency matrix (7.0) supplied their content. Sub-topic codes (6.1.1, ...) and objective codes are ours, not the board's; where the scope lists two short items for the same form they are grouped into one sub-topic. Learning-objective statements are our own paraphrase; no syllabus text is reproduced.
notes: Source (read 2026-10-08): the Mashonaland West provincial education office's copy of the Ministry document, file 'Commerce Form 1-4.pdf' (http://www.mopsemashwest.gov.zw/files/Commerce%20Form%201-4.pdf; the site's https certificate has expired, so the https URL recorded here may not load), read through a text rendering. The cover prints 'Form 1 - 4', '2015-2022' and 'Revised 2015'. The scope-and-sequence and competency-matrix tables come out partly scrambled in the text rendering (column headings unreadable, cells interleaved), so the form in which a sub-topic is taught was read from column positions and cross-checked against the competency matrix (7.1 to 7.38). Check every heading and objective against a clean copy from ZIMSEC and record the exact document URL.
Subject code: not printed in the syllabus document. ZIMSEC O-Level Commerce is commonly cited as 7103; confirm it (code left null).

Version dates: assumed first examined in November 2018 (effectiveFrom 2018-01-01), as for the other 2015-2022 files. Under the Heritage-Based Curriculum (2024-2030) new syllabi were issued; confirm which syllabus the November 2026 and later O-Level Commerce examinations use, set effectiveTo, and create a new version file when a new syllabus replaces this one.

Assessment (8.0) as read: continuous assessment 30% (theory tests, assignments and practical projects over Forms 1 to 4) and a summative examination 70%: Paper 1, 40 multiple-choice questions (1 hour 15 minutes, 40 marks, 20% of the subject); Paper 2, structured questions and essays (2 hours, 100 marks, 50%): Section A, six compulsory structured questions totalling 40 marks; Section B, three essay questions from a choice of seven, totalling 60 marks. The number of options per multiple-choice question and the marks of each structured question are not stated. The assessment-model page says 'The Agriculture learning area will be assessed...', an evident copying slip in the document. Whether calculators are allowed is not stated (calculatorAllowed left out).

Specification grid (8.6) as read through the scrambled rendering: Paper 1 and Paper 2 split across knowledge with understanding, application, analysis and evaluation with totals of 20% and 50%; the individual cell values could not be read reliably.

The document's topic list (5.0) has eleven topics (Production, Trade, Consumer protection, Business organisations, Enterprise, Finance and banking, Insurance and assurance, Business communication, Transport, Warehousing, Marketing) and the scope and sequence uses the same order. Chain of distribution is listed under Production (Form 2); in this family it is the concept bus.marketing.place, shared with the other syllabi.

Organisations named in the competency matrix as examples (telecommunication operators, courier companies, home-industry sites, marketing boards, business membership organisations) date from 2015; content should check that any named organisation still exists and avoid claims about its current market position.

The family also serves ZIMSEC Business Enterprise and Skills and Cambridge IGCSE Business: concepts covered only by those syllabi (for example production methods, break-even analysis, cash flow forecasts, motivation theories, recruitment and the business cycle) are not part of this syllabus.
overview: ZIMSEC O-Level Commerce (Forms 1-4) studies the commercial world in a Zimbabwean context: production and the ownership of the means of production, home and foreign trade, consumer protection, types of business organisation, enterprise, finance and banking (money, personal finance, banks, business finance, the stock exchange and business calculations), insurance and assurance, business communication, transport, warehousing and marketing.
assessmentOverview: Continuous assessment (theory tests, assignments and practical projects, Forms 1-4) carries 30%. The examination carries 70%: Paper 1 has 40 multiple-choice questions (1 hour 15 minutes, 40 marks, 20%) and Paper 2 (2 hours, 100 marks, 50%) has six compulsory structured questions worth 40 marks in Section A and three essays chosen from seven, worth 60 marks, in Section B.

components.name: Paper 1: Multiple choice
components.description: 40 compulsory multiple-choice questions on the whole syllabus.

components.name: Paper 2: Structured questions and essays
components.description: Section A (40 marks): six compulsory structured questions. Section B (60 marks): three essay questions chosen from seven.

children.name: Stages and factors of production
children.description: Form 1: the need for production, goods and services, primary, secondary and tertiary production, factors of production and how commerce relates to production.

objectives.text: Explain why people need production and classify goods and services.
Describe primary, secondary and tertiary production and the chain of production.
Describe the factors of production and their rewards.
Explain how commerce is related to production.

children.name: Ownership of the means of production
children.description: Form 1: the means of production as heritage, land reform and indigenisation.

objectives.text: Explain why local ownership of the means of production is important.
Describe the significance of land as heritage and of land reform and indigenisation for the economy.

children.name: Forms of production, division of labour and mass production
children.description: Form 2: direct and indirect production, division of labour and specialisation, mass production.

objectives.text: Distinguish between direct and indirect production.
Explain the advantages and disadvantages of division of labour and specialisation.
Describe mass production.

children.name: Chain of distribution
children.description: Form 2: channels by which goods reach consumers and how a channel is chosen.

objectives.text: Describe the ways in which goods are distributed from producers to consumers.
Identify factors considered when choosing a channel of distribution.

children.name: Value addition and beneficiation
children.description: Form 3: adding value at each stage of production and the benefits of exploiting local resources.

objectives.text: Explain value addition and beneficiation and how value is added at each stage of production.
Explain how the community and the country benefit when local resources are processed.

children.name: Business environment
children.description: Form 4: internal and external factors affecting a business.

objectives.text: Describe the business environment and its internal and external elements.
Explain how political, economic, social and technological factors affect a business.

children.name: Introduction to trade
children.description: Form 1: reasons for trade, barter and monetary trade, home and foreign trade, branches of trade.

objectives.text: Explain why trade is needed.
Compare barter with trade that uses money.
Compare home trade and foreign trade and illustrate the branches of trade.

children.name: Wholesale trade
children.description: Form 1: services of wholesalers, types of wholesaler, bypassing the wholesaler, marketing boards and commodity markets.

objectives.text: Explain the services wholesalers give to manufacturers, retailers and consumers.
Describe types of wholesaler, including cash and carry and co-operative wholesale societies.
Explain why the wholesaler is sometimes bypassed.
Describe the functions of marketing boards and commodity markets.

children.name: Retail trade
children.description: Form 2: functions and types of retailers, establishing a retail outlet, trends in retailing and the survival of small-scale retailers.

objectives.text: Explain the functions of retailers.
Distinguish between large-scale and small-scale retailers and describe their characteristics.
Describe factors to consider when setting up a retail outlet.
Discuss the impact of trends in retailing such as electronic point of sale, bar coding, vending machines and e-commerce.
Discuss why small-scale retailers survive.

children.name: Hire purchase and deferred payments
children.description: Form 2: hire purchase, deferred payment, credit cards and informal credit.

objectives.text: Explain the main features of hire purchase and deferred payment and compare them.
Identify how hire purchase and credit sales are financed.
Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of buying on credit.

children.name: Discounts and documents used in home trade
children.description: Form 2: trade and cash discounts; the documents used in home trade, their contents and functions.

objectives.text: Explain the purposes of trade and cash discounts, distinguish them and calculate them.
Identify the documents used in home trade and list the contents of each.
Explain the function of each document and complete simple trade documents.

children.name: Foreign trade
children.description: Form 3: interdependence of countries, problems of importers and exporters, entrepot trade, free trade and protection, customs authorities, trading blocs, documents and intermediaries.

objectives.text: Identify the difficulties faced by importers and exporters and explain entrepot trade.
Explain free trade and protectionism and identify methods of restricting trade.
Analyse the functions of customs authorities.
Describe trading blocs and analyse their benefits and challenges.
Describe the purpose and key information of documents used in foreign trade.
Explain the functions of intermediaries in foreign trade and distinguish between them.

children.name: Balance of payments
children.description: Form 4: visible and invisible trade, balance of trade and balance of payments, exchange rates.

objectives.text: Calculate the balance of trade, the invisible balance and the balance of payments.
Outline ways of correcting a balance of payments deficit.
Convert currencies using exchange rates.

children.name: Reasons for consumer protection; consumer rights and responsibilities
children.description: Form 1.

objectives.text: Identify areas in which consumers need protection and ways in which they can be exploited.
Explain consumer rights and the responsibilities of consumers.

children.name: Consumer protection boards
children.description: Form 2: bodies such as the Consumer Council of Zimbabwe and the Standards Association of Zimbabwe.

objectives.text: Identify consumer protection bodies and explain their roles.

children.name: Methods of protecting consumers and the role of government
children.description: Form 3.

objectives.text: Discuss methods of protecting consumers, including legislation.
Explain the role of government in consumer protection.
Identify how consumers can protect themselves.

children.name: Importance of business organisations; business sectors
children.description: Form 1: private and public sectors and the business units in each.

objectives.text: Justify the importance of business organisations.
Describe the private and public sectors and classify business units into them.

children.name: Unincorporated business units
children.description: Form 2: sole proprietorships and partnerships.

objectives.text: Explain the features, formation, ownership and control of unincorporated businesses.
Examine the advantages and disadvantages of unincorporated business units.
Distinguish between a sole proprietorship and a partnership.

children.name: Incorporated business units
children.description: Form 3: private and public limited companies, their formation and documents.

objectives.text: State the types of incorporated business units and describe their formation, ownership and control.
Distinguish between private and public limited companies.
Outline the advantages and disadvantages of incorporated business units.

children.name: Multinational corporations
children.description: Form 3.

objectives.text: Explain the features, advantages and disadvantages of multinational corporations.
Assess the impact of multinational corporations on the host and the parent country.

children.name: Public sector business units
children.description: Form 3: public corporations, local authorities and marketing boards.

objectives.text: State the functions of public sector organisations.
Outline the merits and demerits of public enterprises.

children.name: Traders' associations and business membership organisations
children.description: Form 4.

objectives.text: Identify traders' associations and explain their functions.
Explain the importance of business membership organisations.

children.name: Small to medium enterprises
children.description: Form 4.

objectives.text: Describe the features of small to medium enterprises and explain their importance.
Outline the challenges faced by small to medium enterprises.
Evaluate government programmes for small to medium enterprises.

children.name: Public sector reforms
children.description: Form 4: commercialisation, privatisation and nationalisation.

objectives.text: Define commercialisation, privatisation and nationalisation.
Explain the reasons for and against each reform.

children.name: Introduction to enterprise
children.description: Form 1: qualities of an entrepreneur and the importance of enterprise skills.

objectives.text: Identify the qualities of an entrepreneur.
Explain the advantages and disadvantages of being an entrepreneur.
Evaluate the importance of enterprise skills to the economy.

children.name: Management functions
children.description: Form 2.

objectives.text: Explain the functions of management such as planning, organising, directing and controlling.
Explain the importance of each management function.

children.name: Business ethics
children.description: Form 2.

objectives.text: Identify ethical considerations in business.
Explain the role and importance of ethics in business and society.

children.name: Business plan
children.description: Form 3.

objectives.text: Describe the layout and contents of a business plan and its importance.
Design a business plan for a business idea.

children.name: Intellectual property
children.description: Form 3.

objectives.text: Explain the types of intellectual property and why they are protected.
Suggest solutions to infringements of intellectual property.
Describe the functions of the national patents office and regional and international property organisations.

children.name: Personal finance
children.description: Form 1: sources of income, saving and personal investment.

objectives.text: Explain the sources of personal income.
State methods of saving and justify the need to save.
Identify methods of personal investment and analyse reasons for investing.

children.name: Money
children.description: Form 1: origins, characteristics and functions of money; inflation.

objectives.text: Trace the origins of money.
Describe the characteristics of money and outline its functions.
Discuss the causes and effects of inflation.

children.name: Managing personal finances
children.description: Form 2: budgeting, borrowing options, financial advice and financial mismanagement.

objectives.text: Draw up a personal budget.
Discuss reasons for borrowing and identify borrowing options.
Analyse the need for financial advice and the consequences of financial mismanagement.

children.name: Taxation
children.description: Form 2.

objectives.text: Recognise the legal obligation to pay tax and discuss personal taxes.

children.name: The banking system and commercial banks
children.description: Form 2: classification of banks and commercial banking services.

objectives.text: Identify different types of banks.
Describe the services offered by commercial banks.
Complete banking documents such as cheques, deposit slips and withdrawal slips.

children.name: Business finance
children.description: Form 3: sources of finance, long-term and short-term capital, shares and debentures.

objectives.text: Describe and evaluate the sources of business finance.
Explain long-term and short-term capital.
Distinguish between shares and debentures and between ordinary and preference shares.

children.name: Other financial institutions
children.description: Form 3: merchant banks, finance houses, discount houses, building societies, savings banks and small-enterprise finance institutions.

objectives.text: Outline the services provided by each financial institution.

children.name: The Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe
children.description: Form 3.

objectives.text: Describe and analyse the functions of the Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe.

children.name: Business calculations
children.description: Form 4: working capital, gross and net profit, rate of stock turnover, return on capital employed, mark-up and margin.

objectives.text: Define and calculate working capital, gross profit, net profit, turnover and the rate of stock turnover.
Calculate return on capital employed.
Calculate profit margin and mark-up.

children.name: Zimbabwe Stock Exchange
children.description: Form 4.

objectives.text: Assess the importance of the Zimbabwe Stock Exchange to the economy.
Explain the roles of speculators and outline the functions of brokers and jobbers.

children.name: Trends in banking
children.description: Form 4: telebanking, mobile banking and money transfer agents.

objectives.text: Identify developments in the banking sector.
Evaluate the usefulness of banking trends to the economy.

children.name: International financial institutions
children.description: Form 4.

objectives.text: Outline the international financial institutions and their roles.
Analyse the effectiveness of their activities in Zimbabwe.

children.name: Nature and purpose of insurance and assurance; communal systems
children.description: Form 1: insurance and assurance, risks, pooling of risks, statistics, and communal systems such as zunde ramambo.

objectives.text: Explain the features and purposes of insurance and assurance and distinguish between them.
Identify business and life risks and differentiate insurable from non-insurable risks.
Explain the pooling of risks and the importance of statistics in insurance.
Identify communal systems of insurance and assurance and state their importance.

children.name: Principles of insurance
children.description: Form 2: utmost good faith, indemnity, insurable interest and proximate cause.

objectives.text: Explain the principles of insurance.

children.name: Documents used in insurance and insurance procedures
children.description: Form 2: proposal form, prospectus, cover note and policy; effecting a policy and making a claim; brokers, underwriters, actuaries and assessors.

objectives.text: Identify the documents used in insurance.
Outline the procedure for obtaining a policy and for making a claim.
State the functions of brokers, underwriters, actuaries and assessors.

children.name: Types of insurance and assurance policies; Export Credit Guarantee Corporation
children.description: Form 3: insurance policies, assurance policies, the National Social Security Authority and export credit guarantee.

objectives.text: Explain the types of insurance policies.
Examine the benefits of insurance and assurance policies.
Explain the reasons for the formation of the National Social Security Authority.
Explain the purpose of the Export Credit Guarantee Corporation.

children.name: Impact of ICT on insurance and assurance
children.description: Form 4.

objectives.text: Explain e-insurance and e-assurance.
State the advantages and disadvantages of ICT in insurance and assurance.

children.name: Importance of communication
children.description: Form 1 (with the choice of mode of communication from Form 3).

objectives.text: Explain the term communication and outline its importance.
Outline factors to consider in choosing a mode of communication.

children.name: Telecommunication and service providers
children.description: Form 1.

objectives.text: Describe types of telecommunication devices and services and their advantages and disadvantages.
Identify telecommunication service providers and the services they provide.

children.name: Postal services
children.description: Form 2.

objectives.text: Identify agents of postal services and describe the postal services offered.
Explain the importance and drawbacks of postal services.

children.name: Effective communication
children.description: Form 2: enhancers of and barriers to effective communication.

objectives.text: Explain the importance of effective communication and identify what enhances it.
Outline barriers to communication and suggest ways of overcoming them.

children.name: Formal and informal communication; trends in business communication
children.description: Form 3.

objectives.text: Distinguish between formal and informal business communication and identify their advantages and disadvantages.
Draft a business letter.
Assess the impact of technological developments on business communication.

children.name: Importance and modes of transport
children.description: Form 1.

objectives.text: Explain the importance of transport in commercial activities and trace its development.
Examine the advantages and disadvantages of each mode of transport.

children.name: Choice of transport, transport documents and port authorities
children.description: Form 2.

objectives.text: Discuss the factors that influence the choice of transport.
List the documents used in transport and outline the contents of each.
Describe the services provided by port authorities.

children.name: Trends in transport
children.description: Form 3: containerisation, toll gates, vehicle tracking, e-ticketing, satellite positioning and air cargo.

objectives.text: Describe containerisation and other developments in transport and assess their impact.
Outline the reasons for the growth of air cargo and discuss the impact of ICT on transport.

children.name: Introduction to warehousing; functions and importance
children.description: Forms 1 and 2: warehousing, indigenous storage systems, and the functions and importance of warehouses.

objectives.text: Describe warehousing and identify indigenous storage systems.
Discuss the importance and functions of warehouses.

children.name: Types of warehouses and location of a warehouse
children.description: Form 3.

objectives.text: Identify types of warehouse.
Select an appropriate site for a warehouse.

children.name: Marketing concepts
children.description: Form 1: the need for marketing and the production, product, selling and marketing concepts.

objectives.text: Justify the need for marketing.
Explain the different marketing concepts and assess their implications for a business.

children.name: Types of markets
children.description: Form 1: physical and virtual markets.

objectives.text: Identify and explain types of markets.
Describe the features and discuss the advantages of physical and virtual markets.

children.name: Market segmentation
children.description: Form 2.

objectives.text: Explain market segmentation and identify bases of segmentation.
Outline reasons for market segmentation.

children.name: Marketing approaches
children.description: Form 2: mass and niche marketing.

objectives.text: Explain mass marketing and niche marketing and distinguish between them.

children.name: Marketing mix
children.description: Form 3: product, price, place and promotion.

objectives.text: Identify and explain the marketing mix variables.
Analyse the impact of each marketing mix variable on the market and the business.
Suggest appropriate products, prices, distribution and promotion for a given market and design an advertisement.
